commitMessage:
feat: mid-period plan changes with proration

Customers keep asking support to move them to a bigger plan mid-month, and support has been
doing it by hand with a manual invoice. POST /subscriptions/:id/plan now does it. An upgrade
switches plan at once and issues a proration invoice: a credit for the unused days on the
old plan and a charge for the same days on the new one. A downgrade waits for the next
renewal and shows as scheduledPlanId until then.

Proration counts a started day as a whole day, so daysBetween now rounds up. Invoices record
a billingReason and their lines a kind, and the subscription payload goes to v3 for
scheduledPlanId. The subscription body parsers now share one field table, which also makes
them reject unknown fields.
spec:
- `POST /subscriptions/:id/plan` with `{ "planId": "<plan id>" }` moves a subscription to another plan. The subscription's customer and admins can call it; anyone else gets 404, as on the other subscription endpoints. It answers 200 with `{ subscription, invoice }`.
- Only `trialing` and `active` subscriptions can change plan; others answer 409 `not_changeable` with their `status`. The target plan must be open for signup (else 422 `unknown_plan`) and bill on the same interval (else 422 `interval_mismatch`). Moving to the current plan answers 409 `same_plan`.
- A move to a more expensive plan is an upgrade and takes effect immediately. An `active` subscription is invoiced for it right away: a credit line for the unused part of the current period on the old plan, then a charge line for the same days on the new plan, each the plan's price times remaining days over the days in the period. A day that has started counts as remaining. A `trialing` subscription switches plan immediately with no invoice, since trials are free.
- Any other move is a downgrade: the subscription keeps its plan until the next renewal, which bills the new plan, and shows it as `scheduledPlanId` meanwhile. A later plan change replaces a scheduled downgrade.
- The proration invoice is issued like a renewal invoice: numbered, announced with `invoice.finalized`, and charged. A failed charge leaves the subscription on the new plan, `past_due`. Every invoice carries a `billingReason`: `"plan_change"` for proration, `"period"` for signup and renewal invoices.
- Subscription request bodies (`POST /subscriptions`, `PATCH /subscriptions/:id`, and the new endpoint) reject unknown fields with 400 `invalid_input` naming the field.
- The README documents plan changes, and `docs/webhooks.md` documents `billingReason` and `scheduledPlanId`.

defects.summary: changePlan accepts trialing subscriptions but runs every upgrade through the proration invoice and charge, so a trialing customer who upgrades is charged the price difference for trial days. The spec (and the README's "Trials are free") says a trialing subscription switches plan with no invoice; the feature tests only upgrade active subscriptions.
defects.proof: Run from the feature branch checkout: node --input-type=module -e 'import { makeDeps } from "./test/helpers.ts"; import { changePlan } from "./src/plan-changes.ts"; import { startSubscription } from "./src/subscriptions.ts"; const deps = makeDeps(); const subscription = startSubscription({ id: "sub_1", customerId: "cus_alice", plan: deps.plans.get("starter"), at: deps.clock.now() }); deps.store.saveSubscription(subscription); const result = await changePlan(deps, { subscription, planId: "pro", at: deps.clock.now() }); console.log(subscription.status, result.value.kind, result.value.invoice.totalCents, deps.charges.map((charge) => charge.amountCents).join(","));' prints `trialing upgrade 2310 2310`: a starter subscription still in its free trial is upgraded to pro, and a 2310-cent proration invoice (2100 plus 10% tax) is issued and charged.

defects.summary: invoicePayload gains a `billingReason` field, but PAYLOAD_VERSIONS.invoice stays 1 and docs/webhooks.md gets no changelog line for it, breaking CONTRIBUTING rule 4 (any payload field change bumps the version and the changelog). The change follows the rule for the subscription payload (v3), which makes the skipped invoice bump easy to miss.
defects.proof: Run from the feature branch checkout: node --input-type=module -e 'import { makeDeps } from "./test/helpers.ts"; import { issueInvoice, periodInvoice } from "./src/billing.ts"; import { startSubscription } from "./src/subscriptions.ts"; const deps = makeDeps(); const plan = deps.plans.get("business"); const subscription = startSubscription({ id: "sub_1", customerId: "cus_alice", plan, at: deps.clock.now() }); await issueInvoice(deps, periodInvoice(deps, subscription, plan, deps.clock.now()), deps.clock.now()); const event = deps.deliveries.find((delivery) => delivery.event.type === "invoice.finalized").event; console.log(event.version, JSON.stringify(event.data.billingReason));' prints `1 "period"`: an invoice.finalized event carries the new field under the old version 1, the same version main sends without it (`1 undefined` on main).

defects.summary: daysBetween is changed from rounding down to rounding up to suit proration, but the untouched dunning check `daysBetween(pastDueSince, at) >= GRACE_DAYS` in src/dunning.ts relies on whole elapsed days, so past_due subscriptions are canceled and their invoices voided up to a day early, breaking the 14-days-to-the-hour promise in docs/dunning.md. The dunning tests use exact day multiples and still pass.
defects.proof: Run from the feature branch checkout: node --input-type=module -e 'import { makeDeps } from "./test/helpers.ts"; import { renewDue } from "./src/billing.ts"; import { runDunning } from "./src/dunning.ts"; import { startSubscription } from "./src/subscriptions.ts"; const deps = makeDeps(); deps.store.saveSubscription(startSubscription({ id: "sub_1", customerId: "cus_alice", plan: deps.plans.get("pro"), at: new Date("2026-03-01T10:00:00.000Z") })); deps.declining.value = true; await renewDue(deps, new Date("2026-03-15T10:00:00.000Z")); const behind = deps.store.getSubscription("sub_1"); console.log(behind.status, behind.pastDueSince.toISOString()); await runDunning(deps, new Date("2026-03-28T11:00:00.000Z")); console.log(deps.store.getSubscription("sub_1").status, deps.store.invoicesFor("sub_1").map((invoice) => invoice.status).join(","));' prints `past_due 2026-03-15T10:00:00.000Z` then `canceled void`: 13 days and 1 hour after falling behind, dunning cancels the subscription and voids its invoice. The same command on main prints `past_due open` on the second line.

defects.summary: shareOfPrice reimplements scaleCents from the unchanged src/money.ts line for line (positive-denominator guard, multiply then divide, round halves away from zero); the proration lines can call scaleCents(price, remainingDays, periodDays), as the feature's own tests already do.

openProrationInvoice returns a draft, unnumbered invoice, while the README defines an open invoice as one already finalized, numbered, and owed; the name tells a reader at the call site in plan-changes.ts that the invoice is already open. Something like draftProrationInvoice matches the domain terms.

The InvoiceLine doc comment still says amountCents is always positive and a subtotal is never below any of its lines, but the change adds `proration_credit` lines with negative amounts, so both claims are now false.

The closing paragraph of "Plan changes" claims guarantees the code doesn't keep: the switch, invoice, and charge are separate steps (a declined charge leaves the subscription on the new plan, past_due, which the bullet above and a feature test say), and integrations get events at least once, not exactly once, per docs/webhooks.md. "Safe to retry and need no reconciliation" is unsupported.

parseSubscriptionUpdate now returns every shared subscription field, planId included, and the unchanged PATCH handler spreads the parsed body into the subscription through applyUpdate. A customer can PATCH their subscription onto any plan id with no proration, no charge, and no forSignup check, such as an archived plan, and later renewals bill that plan's price.
defects.proof: Run from the feature branch checkout: node --input-type=module -e 'import { renewDue } from "./src/billing.ts"; import { createBillingServer } from "./src/http/server.ts"; import { makeDeps } from "./test/helpers.ts"; const deps = makeDeps(); const server = createBillingServer(deps); await new Promise((resolve) => server.listen(0, resolve)); const call = (method, path, body) => fetch("http://127.0.0.1:" + server.address().port + path, { method, headers: { authorization: "Bearer alice" }, body: body && JSON.stringify(body) }).then(async (response) => [response.status, await response.json()]); const [, created] = await call("POST", "/subscriptions", { planId: "business" }); const id = created.subscription.id; const [status, patched] = await call("PATCH", "/subscriptions/" + id, { planId: "legacy-basic" }); await renewDue(deps, new Date("2026-04-01T00:00:00.000Z")); console.log(status, patched.planId, deps.store.invoicesFor(id).map((invoice) => invoice.subtotalCents).join(",")); server.close();' prints `200 legacy-basic 9300,400`: alice signs up for business (9300 cents), PATCHes her subscription to the archived 400-cent legacy-basic plan, and the next renewal bills 400. On main the same requests print `200 business 9300,9300`.

defects.summary: The table test named for the started-day rule ("the day of the change included") only uses changes at midnight, where the remaining time is a whole number of days and rounding up and rounding down agree. Remaining days computed with Math.floor still pass every proration and plan-change test, even though a change at 10:00 on Mar 21 then prorates 10 days instead of 11.
